candidates: Do not grant `contents: write` (or any repo-write) permission to GitHub Actions workflows. Instead of having CI auto-commit generated changes, add a CI verification check that fails when the uncommitted changes exist, and document the manual step (e.g., in RELEASE.md) for the release manager to run locally before cutting a release.

Pin third-party GitHub Actions to a full immutable commit hash (e.g., `uses: EndBug/add-and-commit@1bad3abcf0d6ec49a5857d124b0bfb52dc7bb081`) rather than a mutable version tag like `@v9`. Rely on Renovate (or a similar bot) to open upgrade PRs when a new hash should be adopted.

When a GitHub Actions workflow must commit or push changes, set the committer/author identity explicitly to `41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com` so the auto-generated origin of the commit is immediately visible in the git log.

In the `packages/mermaid` package, place docs-processing and release-automation scripts under `packages/mermaid/scripts/`, not under `packages/mermaid/src/`. The `src/` directory is for library source code; `scripts/` is for build and release tooling.

When adding a new process or convention reference to the PR checklist (`.github/pull_request_template.md`) or contributing documentation, include a direct hyperlink to the detailed explanation of that convention so contributors can easily find it.

When adding new `push:` event triggers (with branch filters) to an existing GitHub Actions workflow, verify that the pre-existing `pull_request:` and `merge_group:` triggers are still present and unmodified, so PR and merge-queue validation is not inadvertently dropped.

Prefer CI-driven generation of committed documentation artifacts over manually-run local builds. Local environments can produce subtly different output even with lockfiles. If a manual run is unavoidable (e.g., at release time), add a complementary CI verification step that fails when the checked-in output is out of sync with the source.
